content_of_post_to_comment:
I have been preparing for an entrance exam for the past year and a half, and the pressure and workload are brutal. Every week we have a test covering whatever was taught that week, and I have been consistently getting marks that I'm not happy with. I kept thinking, maybe next week. Then the next. Then the next. More than 50 exams so far.

I know I can perform way better, but it's like my mind uses every failed test as evidence that I'm a waste of space, that I'm a pathetic loser who won't amount to anything. I've gotten to the point where I cry myself to sleep almost every day.

I genuinely want to move forward, but my brain feels like it can't handle the uncertainty anymore. It keeps demanding some kind of guarantee that all this effort will actually lead somewhere. And I know that's impossible, which just makes the whole thing worse.

I guess the question now becomes ...

How do you keep moving forward when part of you desperately wants to, but another part of you is exhausted, scared, and doesn't want to let go of the pain and disappointment?
comment: The part about your brain demanding a guarantee really hit me. I think a lot of people get trapped because they treat uncertainty as proof they should stop. After 50+ tests, the goal might not be to feel confident before continuing, but to learn how to keep showing up while confidence is missing. Also, your scores are feedback, not a verdict on your worth.
